name: AWS Account Identity Guard
description: Declared-profile vs. actual-account safety: destructive operations under a prod profile need admin approval, profile switches via AWS_PROFILE, inline static credentials and local profile rewrites need a written reason, destructive commands on ambient credentials draw a warning, and identity checks / cross-account role assumptions are logged for the cross-account exposure report.

rules.name: Require access request for destructive AWS operations under a prod profile
rules.description: A delete/terminate/disable operation with --profile <...prod...> or AWS_PROFILE=<...prod...> is a production change. Requires admin approval. Instead: run it against staging first with an explicit --profile, or request a keycard for the production run.

rules.name: Require access request to assume the root session of a member account
rules.description: sts assume-root grants root-level access to a member account for privileged tasks. Requires admin approval.

rules.name: Require justification to select a prod profile through the environment
rules.description: AWS_PROFILE=<...prod...> as a command prefix or an export switches every following command to production without the --profile flag that other rules key on. Requires a written reason. Instead: pass --profile explicitly on each production command so intent is visible in the audit trail.

rules.name: Require justification for inline static AWS credentials
rules.description: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN set on the command line bypass named profiles, so nobody can tell which account the command hits. Requires a written reason. Instead: aws configure sso or a named profile.

rules.name: Require justification to rewrite local AWS profile configuration
rules.description: aws configure set / import rewrite ~/.aws/config and ~/.aws/credentials — the mapping from a profile name like 'staging' to an actual account. A wrong edit is how a 'staging' profile ends up pointing at production. Requires a written reason.

rules.name: Warn on destructive AWS operations that rely on ambient credentials
rules.description: A delete/terminate/disable command with no --profile (and no AWS_PROFILE prefix) runs against whatever the default credential chain resolves to — the classic wrong-account incident. Records a warning. Instead: add --profile <name> and run aws sts get-caller-identity first.

rules.name: Warn on cross-account role assumption
rules.description: sts assume-role crosses an account boundary; recording it is what the cross-account exposure report is built from. Records a warning without blocking.

rules.name: Log identity checks before AWS actions
rules.description: aws sts get-caller-identity is the developer verifying which account they are in. Logging it gives the account-identity check its evidence trail. Does not block or warn.
